transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, thank you. I guess the main thing is my sleep has been kind of off lately. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but some nights I’m up half the night and my mind just won’t slow down, and other times I wake up really early and feel like I didn’t rest at all. I figured it might be worth talking to someone about.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized or high, even when you weren’t sleeping much?

Yeah… I mean, I guess there have been a few times like that. Not a lot, or at least I don’t think so. But there were several nights where I only slept maybe three or four hours, and then I still got up feeling kind of charged, like I didn’t even need coffee. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
During those times when you slept only three or four hours and still felt charged, did you also feel unusually high or euphoric?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t know if I’d call it euphoric exactly, but earlier this month I felt kind of… lit up, I guess. Like unusually confident, like I could handle anything. It felt good at first.

But then I also got kind of short with people. I snapped at my mom and even my supervisor over really small questions, which normally I’d just answer and move on. I’m not proud of that, but it did happen.
During that lit-up period, did you find yourself starting a lot more projects or activities than usual?

Yeah… I guess I did. I mean, I was still going to work and everything, so it wasn’t like I was totally out of control, but after work I’d come home and suddenly be cleaning a bunch, making lists for things I wanted to renovate, checking interest rates, even trying to set up ideas for side jobs.

It felt productive at the time, honestly… like I was finally getting things together. But looking back, it was a lot, and I kind of couldn’t shut it off. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During that lit-up period, did other people notice that you were acting unusually different from your normal self?

A little, yeah. My sister noticed, mostly. She said I was talking really fast — like about equity and taxes and then suddenly paint colors — and she couldn’t really get a word in.

I don’t think I meant to be rude or anything… I just felt like if I stopped talking I’d lose the thread, so I kept pushing to keep going. I guess that was pretty different for me.
During that lit-up period, did it ever get so severe that you had to be hospitalized?
No, no hospitalization or anything like that. It didn’t get to that point. I mean, it felt intense, but I was still… you know, functioning enough. So I don’t think it was that severe.
About how many days in a row did that lit-up period last?

Um… the really noticeable up-and-down part has been about a month, I think, since the mortgage stuff became real. 

The “lit-up” stretch itself was several days in a row at a time… I’m sorry, I don’t know if that’s specific enough. It wasn’t just one day, though. It kind of stood out as part of this past month of cycling between that charged-up feeling and then crashing after.
During that lit-up period, did you do anything more risky or impulsive than usual?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in any big way, at least. I mean, I might’ve been a little more quick to say yes to things or get ahead of myself, but I’m not sure I’d call it risky.

I’m trying to be honest — I just don’t want to make it sound worse than it was. If you mean like really dangerous stuff, then no, I don’t think I did anything like that.
During that lit-up period, did it cause serious problems at work or in your relationships?

Um… I wouldn’t say it, like, ruined anything, but… yeah, I guess it has caused some problems.

I’m still going to work, I haven’t stopped showing up or anything, but I’ve made more reconciliation mistakes than I normally would. Enough that my supervisor pulled me aside, which was really embarrassing. And with people… I’ve kind of been avoiding salsa class and my friends because I just don’t feel like myself. I don’t know if that counts as serious, but it’s definitely not normal for me.
Did that energized, unusually confident period last at least 4 days in a row?

I think so, yes… at least, the really obvious part wasn’t just a day or two. The whole back-and-forth between feeling charged up and then crashing has been going on about a month, since the mortgage stuff got real.

So… I’m not trying to overstate it, but yes, there were stretches that felt like several days in a row.
During this past month, have you had a period where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but lately I’ve been waking up with this really heavy, empty feeling. Like even sitting in my own condo — which I worked so hard for — it just… makes me want to cry sometimes.

So yes, I guess that’s been there a lot of the day, most days.
During this past month, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, maybe not completely, but I’ve definitely pulled back from things I normally like.

I stopped going to salsa class, which is kind of embarrassing because I usually really enjoy it. And my paints are still sitting out on the table at home, but I just… look at them and feel nothing. Like they belong to somebody else or something.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but… yes, I think I have.
During this past month, have you felt unusually tired or low in energy nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I still get into bed and sleep, so part of me feels like I shouldn’t complain, but even after a full night, I wake up already tired.

Like just walking from the parking lot into the office feels heavier than it should, like I’m dragging sandbags or something. And by lunch my brain feels… worn out. Is that the kind of low energy you mean?
During this past month, have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty?

A little, yeah… I mean, I know logically it’s probably not fair to say, but I keep telling myself I was stupid to take on the mortgage. Like I should’ve known better or been more careful.

And then I get this feeling like I’ve let everyone down, even though… no bill is actually late or anything. So it feels kind of irrational saying it out loud, but it’s been in my head a lot. Is that what you mean?
During this past month, have you had thoughts that life wasn’t worth living or thoughts of killing yourself?

Um… no, I don’t think so. Not like… killing myself or making a plan or anything.

I mean, I’ve had moments where I feel really overwhelmed and kind of wish I could just not have to deal with everything for a while, but I don’t think I’ve thought that life wasn’t worth living. Is that… is that an okay distinction?
During those energized periods, did your thoughts feel like they were racing?

Yeah… I think they did, though I don’t want to make it sound dramatic.

It was like my mind would jump really fast from one thing to another — mortgage payments, then my CPA study schedule, then suddenly kitchen cabinets or some other project — and I couldn’t slow it down enough to just relax. I’d try to settle myself, but my brain wouldn’t really cooperate.

Is that what you mean by racing thoughts?
